tasks.short: Turn Finance Director budget instructions into clear rules for all three sites.

today.trigger: The Finance Director issues annual budget instructions or changes assumptions during a forecast round.
steps: Read the instructions and compare them with existing SharePoint budget policies.
Check implications for site budgets, agency labour, CAO increases and capital spending.
Resolve unclear assumptions with the Finance Director, Controller and relevant HR specialists.
Update Excel templates and draft guidance with worked examples.
Circulate the approved version and answer budget owners' questions.
drudgery: Answering the same interpretation questions across three sites.
today.time_sinks: Finding the authoritative version, reconciling inconsistent wording and correcting templates after assumptions change.

lenses.faster: Compare new instructions with approved rules automatically and draft the changed guidance, examples and template updates. The analyst spends time resolving ambiguity and checking consequences.
lenses.autonomous: A new directive in a designated SharePoint library triggers a comparison and a draft review pack. Approved rules can then drive deterministic template checks.
lenses.ambitious: Give each site guidance tailored to its labour mix and cost structure, with examples and checks before submissions arrive.
lenses.joy: Remove document comparisons, repeated copying and routine clarification replies. Keep the conversations that make budget rules understandable and workable.
lenses.options: Show alternative interpretations of ambiguous instructions, with their budget effects and the questions needed to resolve them.
lenses.altitude: Own a versioned set of budget assumptions and validation rules, and improve it using recurring submission errors.
reach: Help the Controller maintain budget submission controls.
Help HR translate approved CAO cost assumptions into consistent financial planning inputs.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst interprets management intent, recognises when a rule will distort site behaviour and negotiates a workable interpretation. The Finance Director retains policy approval.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: language comparison and drafting are useful, but choosing policy and resolving conflicting instructions require accountable judgment. Deterministic software should apply approved numerical rules.

in_practice.trigger: A designated owner adds a new budget directive to the controlled SharePoint library.
steps: Retrieve the directive, previous approved policy and relevant templates within the user's access rights.
Draft a source-linked change table separating explicit instructions, inferred implications and unresolved questions.
Calculate example impacts using approved CAO and finance assumptions in Excel.
Prepare revised guidance and proposed template validation rules.
After human approval, publish the versioned guidance and run regression checks on affected templates.
in_practice.human_gate: The FP&A Analyst checks every interpretation and calculation; the Finance Director approves policy changes before publication. HR or legal reviews workforce provisions where needed, including any applicable OR process.
data_needed: Current and previous approved budget directives.
Existing templates, account mappings and policy owners.
Approved CAO increases, employer cost assumptions and effective dates.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint budget policy register containing source versions, draft changes, calculation checks and named approvals.

evidence.claim: Excel Power Query can import and reshape structured assumption tables to reduce repeated manual preparation.
A language model can draft document comparisons and guidance, but interpretation quality requires source checking.
A 40% time reduction is a provisional estimate for Noordhaven, not a measured result.

risks: A draft may confuse a management preference with a binding policy or CAO requirement.
An outdated effective date or employer cost assumption could affect every site budget.
Uncontrolled publication could leave sites using different policy versions.
Approval waiting time may limit end-to-end speed gains even when drafting becomes faster.
research_questions: How much of the current 101 hours per FTE is document handling versus interpretation, discussion and approval waiting?
Can all three sites use one controlled assumption table and template version?
Does a pilot correctly identify every material change in two previous budget rounds?
Who must approve each policy category, and which workforce changes require an OR process?

tasks.short: Compare warehouse and transport investments, operating changes and financing options.

today.trigger: A site requests spending, proposes an operating change or asks whether to buy, lease or defer an investment.
steps: Clarify the decision, alternatives, baseline and expected operational benefits with the requester.
Collect AFAS costs, supplier quotes, financing terms and operational assumptions.
Build an Excel comparison covering cash flows, payback, net present value and sensitivities.
Challenge volumes, labour savings, implementation costs and service effects with site management.
Write a recommendation and present it to the relevant decision maker.
drudgery: Extracting prices and terms from quotations.
Reconciling units, dates and cost categories across sources.
Reformatting sensitivity tables and decision papers.
today.time_sinks: Incomplete requests, unsupported benefit assumptions and repeated model changes when quotes or financing terms change.

lenses.faster: Extract quote terms into a standard input table and run a tested financial model. Generate the comparison and sensitivity tables without rebuilding the workbook.
lenses.autonomous: A complete investment request triggers data retrieval, calculations and a draft recommendation. Missing inputs or failed checks return the request for clarification.
lenses.ambitious: Assess smaller requests consistently and revisit approved projects to compare realised benefits with the original case.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet reconstruction and presentation formatting. Keep challenging whether benefits are achievable and helping managers choose.
lenses.options: Compare buy, lease, outsource, defer and do nothing, where each is feasible. Show demand, wage and agency-rate sensitivities alongside the base case.
lenses.altitude: Own the investment evaluation method, model controls and feedback from realised outcomes.
reach: Support the Controller with investment appraisal controls and benefit tracking.
Prepare financing comparisons for the Finance Director.
Help site managers turn operational proposals into complete financial requests.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst tests whether operational savings can actually become cash or useful capacity, weighs service and implementation risks, and exposes optimism in proposals.
tasks.pattern_why: Agent with gate: software can produce nearly all of a standard appraisal using approved assumptions. A language model extracts and drafts; deterministic calculations and human approval protect the final recommendation.

in_practice.trigger: A site submits a complete investment request with supporting quotes to a controlled SharePoint intake.
steps: Validate required fields and retrieve authorised financial and operating inputs.
Extract quote and financing terms into a source-linked table, flagging uncertain values for review.
Run a versioned calculation model with approved discount rates, tax treatment and consistent cash flow timing.
Calculate feasible alternatives and sensitivities, checking units, totals and double-counted benefits.
Draft a decision paper showing assumptions, exclusions, break-even points and outstanding risks.
Route the pack for analyst review and delegated spending approval, then schedule a benefits review.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates extracted terms and model outputs; the site owner confirms operational assumptions. The Controller checks material accounting or tax treatment, and the authorised budget holder approves the decision.
systems: Microsoft Excel or a tested calculation service
data_needed: Supplier quotes, financing schedules and contract conditions.
Baseline costs, demand and available operational volume data.
Approved CAO rates, agency rates and employer cost assumptions.
Implementation costs, useful lives, residual values and benefit timing.
Approved discount rates, tax assumptions and spending authority limits.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint investment register containing source documents, input snapshots, model versions, validation results, approvals and benefits reviews.

evidence.claim: Excel provides NPV, XNPV, IRR and what-if analysis capabilities for repeatable financial comparisons.
evidence.source: Microsoft Excel financial functions and What-If Analysis

evidence.claim: Language models can extract proposed commercial terms and draft appraisals around checked calculations; a complete Noordhaven workflow would require implementation.
A 65% time reduction is a provisional estimate for standard requests with complete inputs.

risks: Reduced labour hours may represent spare capacity rather than a cash saving.
Incorrect VAT, financing, residual-value or cash-flow treatment could reverse the ranking.
Supplier claims or extracted contract terms may be incomplete or misleading.
Unusual investments and long approval cycles could deliver substantially smaller speed gains.
research_questions: What share of requests fits a small set of repeatable models, and how often are submissions complete?
Can the workflow reproduce previous approved appraisals without material calculation or extraction errors?
Which claimed benefits were realised in past projects, and which only created unused capacity?
Do measured request-to-decision times support the estimated speedup after approval delays are included?

tasks.short: Find practical ways to lower site costs and improve margins.

today.trigger: A forecast miss, margin decline, management request or recurring performance review prompts an investigation.
steps: Review Power BI trends and reconcile material movements to AFAS.
Combine cost data with available volumes, agency hours and site explanations.
Separate price, volume, mix, timing and productivity effects.
Discuss possible causes and improvements with site managers and Finance.
Estimate benefits, propose a trial and track agreed actions.
drudgery: Downloading and joining recurring cost and agency reports.
Rebuilding variance bridges for each site.
Chasing explanations and updating action trackers.
Reformatting the same findings for monthly reviews.
today.time_sinks: Missing operational denominators, inconsistent site definitions and investigating accounting timing differences that resemble operating problems.

lenses.faster: Refresh reconciled cost and volume comparisons automatically and draft explanations for material exceptions. The analyst starts with checked signals and tests the likely causes.
lenses.autonomous: After each successful nightly extract, rules identify persistent exceptions and prepare investigation packs. Site-specific thresholds and human triage control which findings become actions.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling opportunity pipeline across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, with measured trials and benefits reflected in the forecast only when supported.
lenses.joy: Remove recurring report assembly and tracker maintenance. Keep the site conversations, problem solving and visible improvements.
lenses.options: For each issue, compare feasible actions such as overtime reduction, agency-mix changes, process changes or equipment investment. Show service, safety and implementation trade-offs.
lenses.altitude: Design the process that detects opportunities, tests interventions and distinguishes realised benefits from hopeful estimates.
reach: Help the Controller explain operational margin movements.
Support site managers with trial measurement and financial benefit tracking.
Work with People Analytics on aggregate labour cost drivers and planning assumptions.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst distinguishes correlation from a workable intervention, earns site managers' trust and balances cost with service, safety and workforce constraints.
tasks.pattern_why: Copilot: rules and calculations can surface exceptions, while a language model prepares hypotheses and investigation packs. Selecting an intervention requires operational evidence and human judgment.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract passes reconciliation checks and the required agency and operational inputs are available.
steps: Refresh a governed site-level dataset and check completeness, definitions and reconciliation.
Calculate cost drivers and variance bridges using explicit formulas and agreed materiality thresholds.
Rank persistent exceptions, separating accounting timing issues from potential operational changes.
Draft source-linked hypotheses, missing-data questions and alternative interventions.
Have the analyst and site owner select a trial with a baseline, service safeguards and benefit measure.
Track observed results and submit supported forecast changes through the normal approval process.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates the signal and the site owner authorises operational trials. HR and the applicable OR process are involved where changes affect workforce arrangements; Finance approves forecast adjustments.
systems: Staffing agency exports or authorised interfaces
data_needed: Reconciled costs, revenue, accruals and cost-centre mappings.
Agency hours, rates and invoices from all three agencies.
Available throughput, service, quality and capacity measures with consistent site definitions.
Approved labour assumptions, operational constraints and seasonal calendars.
Trial baselines, implementation costs and action ownership.
in_practice.logs_to: A restricted SharePoint opportunity register linked to Power BI, recording evidence, hypotheses, trial approvals, observed benefits and forecast treatment.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled refresh and rule-based dashboard alerts, subject to configuration and supported data sources.
evidence.source: Microsoft Power BI scheduled refresh and data alerts

evidence.claim: Governed variance calculations and model-assisted hypotheses can reduce investigation preparation, but cannot establish causality by themselves.
A 35% time reduction is a provisional estimate; realised profit improvement has not been established.

risks: AFAS and agency data alone cannot establish warehouse or transport productivity without reliable operational volumes.
Different customer mixes, service requirements or accrual timing could make site comparisons misleading.
Recommendations could reduce service or safety, or shift costs elsewhere.
Employee-level analysis would require a separate AVG/GDPR and applicable EU AI Act assessment; the proposed workflow uses aggregate site and cost data.
research_questions: Are comparable throughput, service and quality measures available for all three sites, and who owns them?
Can current reports separate rate, volume, mix, productivity and accounting timing effects reliably?
How many flagged exceptions lead to actions with measurable benefits rather than explanations alone?
Can a controlled trial demonstrate savings without worsening service, safety or workforce outcomes?

role.altitude: Become the owner of financial decision methods and the operational assumptions behind a forecast the business trusts. Spend more time testing drivers and challenging decisions, supported by repeatable calculations and traceable evidence.
reach: Controller: maintain variance methods, investment appraisal controls and benefit validation.
Finance Director: prepare financing scenarios and evidence for capital allocation.
Site management: design financially measurable operational trials.
People Analytics and HR: translate aggregate labour and CAO assumptions into financial scenarios.
role.ceiling_note: These tasks cover about 17% of the role's stated annual time. Across two FTE, the provisional savings total about 250 hours annually, worth approximately EUR 20,000 of capacity at EUR 80/hour, not an automatic cash saving. End-to-end gains depend on data availability and approval delays; operational judgment, policy authority and implementation remain human responsibilities.
skills_to_grow: Build and validate reusable financial calculation models.
Manage data definitions, reconciliation and source traceability.
Design sensitivities, operational trials and credible benefits measures.
Challenge assumptions and explain uncertainty to site managers.
Configure model-assisted workflows with access controls and clear approval boundaries.
role.ambitious_version: Run a continuous financial decision service across all three sites: maintain approved assumptions, prepare comparable investment options, detect emerging cost pressures and feed verified operational changes into forecasts. Measure success through forecast accuracy, decision turnaround and realised benefits.
